thread:
Tara Gomez: Quick UX flag from QA: on very narrow widths (~300px) the results table body gets an extra horizontal scrollbar after the left rail auto-collapses. It only happens when a long ID and the action toolbar are both visible. Screenshot: https://staging.redwood.internal/ux/shot-599.png

Owen Hale: Reproduced on iPhone SE. The left rail collapse triggers a width animation and the table recalculates mid-frame, so scrollWidth spikes.

Priya Singh: Accessibility note: keyboard users lose visible focus because the focused cell can be pushed out of the scroll container. We should ensure focus is restored and announced.

Ravi Shah: Two low-friction fixes: 1) clamp() / min-width on the first column to avoid long strings driving layout, 2) make the toolbar position: sticky so wrapping doesn't shift document flow. Prefer CSS-only if possible.

Tara Gomez: Also copy UX: users mostly copy IDs. Replace "Show more" with a tiny copy button in the first column for mobile. That avoids opening a popover on tap.

Owen Hale: CSS sample I'm testing: ```css
.row-id { min-width: 88px; max-width: clamp(72px, 30vw, 160px); overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; }
.header-toolbar { position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: 6; }
.main { contain: layout; }
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) { .sidebar { transition: width 160ms ease; } }
```
Will push to staging for a quick smoke.

Priya Singh: For a11y: keep a visually-hidden full-text for screen readers (aria-label on the cell), add an aria-live toast for copy, and don't hide labels entirely for SRs.

ScreenReader-Bot: Tip: aria-label="Full ID: 0xabc... (copy)" and announce "Copied ID" to aria-live.

Ravi Shah: Perf note: avoid JS reflow hacks. If we need scrollIntoView for keyboard users do it in RAF and only when focus changed.

Tara Gomez: Assigning @Owen to land the CSS tweak and the inline copy button, @Priya to review accessibility. If staging looks good, promote to canary tomorrow.

Owen Hale: Will open a small PR with visual diffs for 320px/360px and an integration test that asserts no horizontal scroll on 320px.
